questions.stem_md:
A survey map is drawn to the scale $1 : 25\,000$. Show all working.

(a) A canal path measures $3.8$ cm on the map. Find its real length in km.

(b) A rectangular field measures $5.6$ cm by $3.2$ cm on the map. Find its real area in km$^2$ and in hectares ($1$ km$^2 = 100$ hectares).

(c) The map is redrawn so that the field now covers $4.48$ cm$^2$. Find the new scale, and the length on the new map of a road that is $2.8$ km long.

answer.model_answer_md:
**(a)** Real length $= 3.8 \times 25\,000$: $3.8 \times 25000 = 95000$ cm $= \dfrac{95000}{100000} = 0.95$ km.

**(b)** $1$ cm on the map is $25\,000$ cm $= 0.25$ km. The field is $5.6 \times 0.25$: $5.6 \times 0.25 = 1.4$ km by $3.2 \times 0.25$: $3.2 \times 0.25 = 0.8$ km. Area: $1.4 \times 0.8 = 1.12$ km$^2$, which is $1.12 \times 100 = 112$ hectares.

**(c)** The old map area was $5.6 \times 3.2 = 17.92$ cm$^2$. The area ratio is $\dfrac{4.48}{17.92} = \dfrac{1}{4}$, so the ratio of lengths is $\sqrt{\dfrac{1}{4}} = \dfrac{1}{2}$. Every length is halved, so the new scale is $1 : 50\,000$: $2 \times 25000 = 50000$. A road of $2.8$ km $= 280\,000$ cm measures $\dfrac{280000}{50000} = 5.6$ cm on the new map.

questions.solution_md: Map lengths are multiplied by the scale denominator; areas by its square; the ratio of areas on the two maps is the square of the ratio of lengths.

questions.stem_md:
A town hall displays a scale model of a lighthouse at the scale $1 : 40$. Show all working.

(a) The model is $90$ cm high. Find the height of the real lighthouse in metres.

(b) The glass of the real lamp room has an area of $24$ m$^2$. Find the area of the glass on the model, in cm$^2$.

(c) The model's fuel tank holds $300$ cm$^3$. Find the volume of the real tank in cubic metres, and state the ratio of the two volumes.

answer.model_answer_md:
**(a)** Real height $= 90 \times 40$: $90 \times 40 = 3600$ cm $= \dfrac{3600}{100} = 36$ m.

**(b)** Areas are in the ratio of the squares of lengths: $40^2 = 1600$. Real area $= 24 \text{ m}^2$: $24 \times 10000 = 240000$ cm$^2$, so the model glass has area $\dfrac{240000}{1600} = 150$ cm$^2$.

**(c)** Volumes are in the ratio of the cubes of lengths: $40 \times 40 \times 40 = 64000$. Real volume $= 300 \times 64\,000$: $300 \times 64000 = 19200000$ cm$^3$, that is $\dfrac{19200000}{1000000} = 19.2$ m$^3$. The ratio of the model's volume to the real volume is $1 : 64\,000$.

questions.solution_md: Real lengths are 40 times the model lengths; areas 1600 times; volumes 64 000 times; then convert units.

questions.stem_md:
In $\triangle ABC$, $\angle B = 90^\circ$, $AB = 6$ cm, $BC = 8$ cm and $AC = 10$ cm. In $\triangle PQR$, $\angle Q = 90^\circ$, $PQ = 9$ cm and $QR = 12$ cm. Show all working.

(a) Show that $\triangle ABC \sim \triangle PQR$ and state the condition used.

(b) Find $PR$.

(c) Find the area of $\triangle PQR$ from the area of $\triangle ABC$ using the ratio of areas, and the perimeter of $\triangle PQR$ using the ratio of perimeters.

answer.model_answer_md:
**(a)** $\dfrac{AB}{PQ} = \dfrac{6}{9} = \dfrac{2}{3}$ and $\dfrac{BC}{QR} = \dfrac{8}{12} = \dfrac{2}{3}$, and $\angle B = \angle Q = 90^\circ$. The sides including the equal angles are proportional, so $\triangle ABC \sim \triangle PQR$ by the SAS condition, with $A \to P$, $B \to Q$, $C \to R$.

**(b)** The scale factor from $ABC$ to $PQR$ is $\dfrac{3}{2}$, so $PR = \dfrac{3}{2} \times 10 = 15$ cm. Check with Pythagoras: $9^2 + 12^2 = 225 = 15^2$.

**(c)** Area of $\triangle ABC = \dfrac{1}{2} \times 6 \times 8 = 24$ cm$^2$. The area ratio is $\left(\dfrac{3}{2}\right)^2 = \dfrac{9}{4}$, so area of $\triangle PQR = 24 \times \dfrac{9}{4} = 54$ cm$^2$. Perimeter of $\triangle ABC$: $6 + 8 + 10 = 24$ cm; perimeters are in the ratio $2 : 3$, so the perimeter of $\triangle PQR$ is $24 \times \dfrac{3}{2} = 36$ cm.

questions.solution_md: SAS similarity from the proportional sides around the right angles; the third side scales the same way; areas go as the square of the scale factor and perimeters as the scale factor.
